about.heading: What rhinoplasty is.
about.body: Rhinoplasty reshapes the nose: the bridge, the tip, the nostrils, or all of them. In a closed rhinoplasty the cuts are inside the nostrils. An open rhinoplasty adds a small cut between them, which gives the surgeon a clearer view of the cartilage. If the septum is crooked, it can be straightened in the same operation to help breathing.

measure.heading: The nasal analysis and its published references.
measure.subtext: The simulator measures these on the patient's photo. Each table gives the published reference, the group it was published for, and its source.
measure.legend: Ideal: an author's target range. Point ideal: one published value with no range. Observed: the spread measured in that group, not a target. * The simulator estimates one landmark of this reading. â€  From a secondary source; check the original.
measure.caveat: References are textbook norms, drawn mostly from Caucasian populations. Use them as reference points for discussion, not as targets for every patient.
measure.guides: Also drawn in the simulator as guides, with no reference listed: {names}.
measure.side: In the simulator, side-view angles are measured on a profile photo like this one. The table below gives their published references.

nasofrontal.name: Nasofrontal angle
nasofrontal.body: The angle at the nasion between the forehead and the bridge.

nasolabial.name: Nasolabial angle
nasolabial.body: The angle between the columella and the upper lip.

nasomental.name: Nasomental angle
nasomental.body: The angle at the tip between the nasion and the chin.

goode.name: Goode ratio
goode.body: Tip projection divided by nasal length.

totalProjection.name: Total projection
totalProjection.body: Alar crease to tip, against nasion to tip.

intrinsicProjection.name: Intrinsic projection
intrinsicProjection.body: How far the tip lobule projects beyond the columella.

tipRotation.name: Tip rotation
tipRotation.body: The angle of the tip, measured at the alar crease from the vertical.

columellar.name: Columellar parallelism
columellar.body: Whether the tip axis runs parallel to the columella.

nasalLength.name: Nasal length
nasalLength.body: Nasion to tip, against midface height.

dorsalLine.name: Dorsal line
dorsalLine.body: Bridge height against the line from nasion to tip, to show a hump or a dip.

tipPoint.name: Tip-defining point
tipPoint.body: The most projected point of the tip, marked as a reference.

alarIC.name: Alar to intercanthal ratio
alarIC.body: Nostril base width against the distance between the inner eye corners.

symmetry.name: Nose symmetry
symmetry.body: How far the nasal axis leans off the face midline, with a mirror mismatch score.

nasalThirds.name: Nasal thirds
nasalThirds.body: The nose split into upper, middle and lower thirds, to locate a deviation.

dorsalAesthetic.name: Dorsal aesthetic lines
dorsalAesthetic.body: The brow-to-tip lines that frame the bridge.

facialThirds.name: Facial thirds and fifths
facialThirds.body: Guide lines for vertical and horizontal facial proportion.

frankfort.name: Frankfort horizontal
frankfort.body: A head-tilt reference, so angles are read from a level head.

adjust.heading: Each control moves one part of the nose.
adjust.subtext: The slider shows its value in millimetres or degrees, inside a fixed range.

dorsalProfile.name: Dorsal height
dorsalProfile.body: Reduces a hump or builds up a low bridge.

bridgeWidth.name: Dorsal width
bridgeWidth.body: Narrows or widens the middle of the bridge.

tipRotation.name: Tip rotation
tipRotation.body: Turns the tip up or down.

tipProjection.name: Tip projection
tipProjection.body: Brings the tip forward or back.

nostrilWidth.name: Alar base width
nostrilWidth.body: Narrows or widens the nostril base.

deviationCorrection.name: Deviation correction
deviationCorrection.body: Moves a crooked nose toward the midline.

adjust.extras: Also: each side adjusted on its own, bony base width for surgeons, four one-tap presets, and a brush for fine edits.

s1.title: Photograph front and side
s1.body: In published studies, side views matched results more often than front views. Take both.

s2.title: Turn on the overlays

s3.title: Adjust together

evidence.heading: What rhinoplasty imaging studies found.
evidence.subtext: These studies used other imaging tools, not Faceify.

punthakee.body: of 112 rhinoplasty patients rated the side-view simulation very close to or identical with their result. For the front view, 41.1%.

agarwal.body: of 300 ratings by 12 blinded surgeons judged the simulation a realistic picture of the result, fully or with room to be closer. In 32% it was not.

lekakis.body: of patients who were not offered surgery were unsatisfied with the proposed simulation, against 16% of those who went ahead.

yamamichi.body: correlation between how closely the simulation matched the result and patient satisfaction, across 38 rhinoplasties.

result.q: Does the simulation show the surgical result?
result.a: No. It shows a proposed change on the patient's photo so you can agree on direction and degree. It does not model healing, skin thickness or cartilage.

photos.a: A well-lit front photo and a true side profile. Side-view measurements such as the nasolabial and nasofrontal angles need the profile.

references.q: Do the reference ranges apply to every patient?
references.a: No. They are textbook norms, drawn mostly from Caucasian populations. Use them as reference points for discussion, not as targets.

camera.q: Can I use a live camera?
camera.a: Yes, for rhinoplasty. Live camera mode shows the change on the patient's face in real time, and the camera frame is processed on the device.

cases.heading: Common nose shapes, each set in the simulator.
cases.subtext: Each case is a different AI-generated face. The after is the simulator's own output, captioned with the controls that made it.
cases.caption: <changes></changes> on an AI-generated face. Simulator output, illustrative only.

dorsalHump.name: Dorsal hump
dorsalHump.body: A bump on the bridge, plainest in profile. Dorsal height lowers it and leaves the tip as it is.

bulbousTip.name: Bulbous tip
bulbousTip.body: A broad, rounded tip with little definition. Tip width narrows the lobule and leaves the bridge as it is.

wideNostrils.name: Wide nostrils
wideNostrils.body: Nostrils that flare wide at the base. Alar base width brings the base in and leaves the tip as it is.

droopingTip.name: Drooping tip
droopingTip.body: A tip that hangs below the line of the bridge, often with age. Tip rotation turns it up and shows more of the columella.

recovery.heading: Recovery, week by week.
recovery.subtext: What most people go through after a first rhinoplasty.
recovery.note: Typical timings from the NHS, ASPS, BAPRAS, Cleveland Clinic and MedlinePlus. Your surgeon's plan comes first.

splint.title: Splint off
splint.body: The splint and stitches come off at about a week, sometimes two. Any packing inside the nose is out within a few days.

work.title: Back to work or school
work.body: Most people are back at a desk or in class within one to two weeks.

bruising.title: Bruising fades
bruising.body: Bruising and redness around the eyes and nose fade over two to three weeks.

exercise.title: Exercise again
exercise.body: Walking is fine within days. Strenuous exercise and contact sports wait four to six weeks. Keep glasses off the bridge until your surgeon says otherwise.

swelling.title: Swelling settles
swelling.body: Most of the swelling is gone within a few months. The tip is the last part to settle.

final.title: The final shape
final.body: The refined result, especially at the tip, is judged at about a year.

cost.heading: What a first rhinoplasty typically costs.
cost.subtext: Typical ranges for a first rhinoplasty. Revision and rib-cartilage work cost more. Your quote depends on the surgeon, the technique and what the fee includes.
cost.source: Compiled from clinic price lists and medical travel sites published in 2025 and 2026. A guide only, not a quote.

prepare.heading: Bring the picture, and your questions.

s1.title: Try the change on your photo
s1.body: Move one part at a time until it looks right to you, then save the before and after to show your surgeon.

s2.title: Check the surgeon
s2.body: Ask about their training, how many rhinoplasties they do, and to see their own before and after photos.

s3.title: Ask what is realistic
s3.body: Show the picture and ask what your skin, cartilage and breathing allow. The simulation is a starting point, not a promise.

s4.title: Ask about the plan
s4.body: Open or closed, what the fee includes, where you recover, and when you come back for checks.

simulation.q: Will my nose look exactly like the simulation?
simulation.a: No. It shows a proposed change on your photo so you and your surgeon can agree on direction and degree. It does not model healing, skin thickness or cartilage.

pain.a: Most people describe soreness and a blocked nose rather than severe pain. Ordinary pain relief usually covers it, and it eases within a few days to a week.

permanent.a: Largely, yes. The change is long-lasting, though your nose keeps ageing with the rest of your face.

breathing.a: Often. If the wall between the nostrils, the septum, is crooked, it can be straightened in the same operation. This is called a septorhinoplasty.

age.q: How old do I need to be?
age.a: Old enough that your nose has finished growing. Many surgeons wait until about 15 to 16 for girls and a little later for boys.

risks.a: Bleeding, infection, a numb nose, trouble breathing, a changed sense of smell, and a result you are not happy with, which sometimes means a second operation. A hole in the septum is a rare risk.

1.a: There is no paid trial period. You can embed the patient simulator widget on your clinic website at no cost and with no time limit. An annual seat is charged once for 12 months of access. Renew manually when the paid period ends; there are no automatic renewal charges.

2.a: Paid access covers available procedure simulators. Some procedures are not yet available for purchase. The procedure picker and checkout confirm availability before payment.

3.a: Real-time simulation processing runs in your browser. Your photo is sent off-device only if you turn on the optional AI photoreal preview or choose to save a simulation to your account. We never use your photo to train any model. Faceify Labs is built on HIPAA-aligned architecture from day one.

4.q: Do I need special hardware or software to install?
4.a: None. Faceify Labs runs entirely in a modern browser on any laptop or desktop. No tablet, scanner, or dedicated hardware required, which is why it costs a fraction of hardware-based alternatives like Canfield Vectra ($15,000+).

5.q: How does Faceify compare to Crisalix?
5.a: Crisalix uses a 3D mobile scanner requiring hardware setup. Faceify Labs is fully browser-native: no hardware, no install, no patient data leaving the room. All 85+ procedures use anatomical mesh modeling. Rhinoplasty runs on a high-density proprietary 3D head mesh; the rest use our 468-point facial mesh.
